newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa considers third mobile phone operation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa considers third mobile phone operation.

text.p: South Africa will commission a study early next year to assess the viability of a third cellular telephone operation, officials said on Thursday.

The study is likely to take four to six months to complete after which South Africa's new telecommunications regulator will give a view on whether a third licence should be granted, said Post and Telecommunications minister Jay Naidoo.
"If the market can absorb it, we should (go ahead)," Naidoo told reporters.
South Africa's mobile telephone market has shown phenomenal growth in the last two years.
State utility Telkom said in its 1996 report that the total number of subscribers had increased by over 50 percent in the year to March 31.
At present market leader is Vodacom, a joint venture between Telkom and Britain's Vodafone Plc. The second operator is MTN, representing other local interests and Cable and Wireless Plc.
